stories.headline: Canada pursues interim trade pact with Washington amid ongoing tariff tensions
stories.summary: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc indicated that reaching an interim agreement with the United States could jumpstart formal review discussions for the CUSMA pact, even as cross-border rhetoric remains hostile. Canadian officials and sources report that the recent U.S. midterm elections have not shifted Washington's stance or eased lingering tariff pressures. Ottawa continues to convene economic advisory committees to determine its strategy ahead of broader negotiations.

stories.headline: Carney wraps Asia summit tour balancing China ties, Taiwan trade, and Ukraine support
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney concluded an extensive diplomatic tour across Asia, holding bilateral discussions with Donald Trump and addressing regional leaders in Shenzhen. While Carney praised China's rapid economic growth as an instructive model, he also confronted Vladimir Putin directly at APEC by condemning Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ottawa confirmed it is advancing a bilateral trade agreement with Taiwan, navigating delicate diplomatic balances with Beijing.

stories.headline: United States sanctions alleged Toronto-based cell of Italian mafia
stories.summary: The United States Department of the Treasury has imposed sanctions against six Canadian men identified as leaders of an alleged Canadian branch of Italy's 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate. U.S. authorities allege the organization runs global narcotics operations and coordinated money laundering through Canadian businesses, including Toronto-area funeral homes. The move blocks their U.S. assets and prohibits financial institutions under American jurisdiction from dealing with the named entities.

stories.headline: Federal government's 2026 budget passes in the House of Commons
stories.summary: Members of Parliament have voted to approve the Liberal government's 2026 federal budget in the House of Commons. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne defended the measures as vital support for the country during an uncertain economic climate. The budget's passage secures legislative authority for the government's major spending commitments and economic initiatives.

articles.author: The Canadian Press
articles.title: Liberals’ 2026 budget passes in House of Commons

stories.headline: MPs clash sharply during committee review of Carney government's major projects bill
stories.summary: House of Commons committee proceedings grew volatile as parliamentarians argued over scheduling weekend sittings to debate Bill C-39. The Carney government's signature major projects legislation has sparked protracted dispute over regulatory timelines and scrutiny. Committee sessions briefly derailed with profanity and gavel strikes as opposition members pushed back against compressed review periods.

stories.headline: Liberals resist calls to split medical assistance in dying legislation for separate votes
stories.summary: Justice Minister Sean Fraser confirmed the government will not separate advance requests from its medical assistance in dying legislation for an independent vote. The stance conflicts with calls from both Conservative MPs and the Liberal chair of the MAID committee, who advocate for distinct votes on advance directives, mental illness, and degenerative diseases. The debate highlights growing parliamentary division as the legislation proceeds toward final voting.

stories.headline: Green Party leader invites federal NDP to explore electoral collaboration
stories.summary: Newly elected Green Party Leader Mike Morrice has written to NDP Leader Avi Lewis proposing structured electoral cooperation between their two federal parties. The initiative aims to unite progressive votes to maximize legislative representation rather than splitting support in competitive ridings. Lewis has not formally agreed to the proposal as the NDP concentrates on key upcoming byelections in Montreal and beyond.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declines to hear class-action appeal for off-reserve Indigenous child welfare
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada has refused to hear an application to certify a class-action lawsuit against the federal government on behalf of Indigenous children taken into non-Indigenous care while living off-reserve. The lawsuit sought parity with multibillion-dollar settlements previously reached for child welfare discrimination experienced on reserves. The top court's decision brings an end to this particular legal path for affected off-reserve families seeking federal compensation.

articles.author: The Canadian Press
articles.title: Top court won't hear bid for class-action lawsuit on behalf of Indigenous children

stories.headline: Police deploy AI models for Canada's most wanted list, leading to immediate arrest
stories.summary: Canadian police services introduced life-sized artificial intelligence models depicting the country's 25 most wanted fugitives to assist the public in identifying suspects. Hours after the high-profile launch at the Toronto Police College, joint RCMP and municipal units arrested Bolton homicide suspect Filmon Fesshaghirgis in Winnipeg. Authorities credit the enhanced technological approach and increased public awareness with generating actionable leads.

stories.headline: Ontario Liberal Party set to announce new leader in ranked-ballot race
stories.summary: Ontario Liberals are set to conclude their leadership race on Saturday, selecting their third leader since the Progressive Conservatives took office in 2018. Members are voting via ranked ballots among four candidates: Lee Fairclough, Navdeep Bains, Stephanie Bowman, and Dylan Marando. The contest marks an effort by the third-place party to rebuild organizational strength and mount a viable challenge in the next provincial campaign.

stories.headline: Former Ontario colleges minister dodges scrutiny over expanding OSAP scandal
stories.summary: Former Ontario minister of colleges and universities Jill Dunlop is refusing to answer questions regarding an expanding scandal involving the Ontario Student Assistance Program. Dunlop oversaw the post-secondary portfolio for three years until earlier this year as administrative and financial discrepancies emerged. Opposition lawmakers continue demanding answers about provincial oversight and the allocation of student financial assistance.

stories.headline: Multiple Ontario education unions vote heavily in favour of strike mandates
stories.summary: Education workers represented by CUPE Ontario and French-language school board teachers have delivered overwhelming strike mandates as provincial contract negotiations progress. These votes expand the coalition of education labour unions possessing strike authorization heading into central bargaining with the province and school boards. While job action is not immediate, the mandates increase leverage for unions pressing on wages, staffing levels, and school support resources.

stories.headline: Ontario Northlander passenger train service set to resume operations after 14-year absence
stories.summary: Ontario Northland has confirmed that the Northlander passenger rail line will officially resume service on December 10, connecting Toronto and Cochrane. The passenger rail link returns after a 14-year hiatus, serving 16 communities across northeastern Ontario. Tickets are scheduled to go on sale on November 26, fulfilling a key provincial transit restoration pledge.

stories.headline: Chow appoints new council committee heads and declines seat on Toronto police board
stories.summary: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow announced her executive committee appointments and leadership rosters as city council commenced its new term. Chow declined an appointment to the Toronto Police Services Board, leaving civilian police oversight to designated council allies while keeping her existing slate of deputy mayors. The committee shuffle also established a dedicated social services committee and placed newly elected councillors into high-profile files such as housing.

stories.headline: Incoming TTC chair vows scrutiny over leadership investigation and budget shortfalls
stories.summary: Newly installed TTC Board Chair Paul Ainslie expressed strong concern over ongoing investigations into senior leadership conduct and commission spending. Ainslie assumes leadership of the transit agency as it grapples with an estimated $397-million operating shortfall alongside operational reliability challenges. The incoming chair affirmed plans to demand accountability and pursue rigorous oversight over transit management and finances.

stories.headline: Federal minister convenes urgent talks to avert sale of Brampton Stellantis facility
stories.summary: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly is holding last-minute emergency discussions with company leadership in an attempt to prevent the sale of the Stellantis automotive plant in Brampton. Government officials concede there is little optimism that the facility's divestment can be averted before corporate plans proceed. A potential sale raises severe concerns for thousands of local manufacturing jobs and the stability of Ontario's automotive supply chain.

articles.title: Little hope of averting Stellantis’ sale ahead of Friday meeting with Joly

stories.headline: Special Investigations Unit charges Halton police officer in Burlington shooting
stories.summary: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has charged Halton Regional Police Constable Evan Zych with four assault and firearm-related offences following the shooting of a 23-year-old man in Burlington. The incident occurred during an attempted traffic interaction outside a local motel, leaving the victim hospitalized with multiple gunshot wounds. The SIU determined there are reasonable grounds to conclude the officer committed criminal offences, initiating formal court proceedings.

stories.headline: Coroner's inquest examines police tactics in fatal shooting of Jamal Francique
stories.summary: A coroner's inquest into the 2020 death of Jamal Francique, a 28-year-old Black man fatally shot by Peel police, heard testimonies from medical experts and supervising officers. A forensic pathologist testified that the severity of the head wound made Francique's survival over several days astonishing. The supervisory officer defended the operation, stating that officers were carrying out what was planned as a routine arrest before circumstances escalated.
